items.sentence: drinks as much water a day as Mumbai
items.caveat: For scale, that is roughly what the Central Park Reservoir holds, though the reservoir was taken out of service in 1993 and no longer supplies anyone.

nyc.label: Daily drinking water delivered to New York City

match.label: Water supplied daily to Mumbai by the BrihanMumbai Municipal Corporation
match.quote: The BrihanMumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) is doing a remarkable job by providing 4,000 million litres of water daily to Mumbaikars.

items.note: Greater Mumbai has about 12 to 13 million people. Department of Environmental Protection water supply page (one billion gallons a day); the BrihanMumbai Municipal Corporation's daily supply of 4,000 million litres as reported by the Free Press Journal in September 2025 (other outlets cite 3,950 to 4,100). Converted at 3.78541 litres per US gallon. The Central Park Conservancy's page says the reservoir 'holds 1 billion gallons of water' and, if it were still in use, would supply the city 'for about one day'. It was decommissioned in 1993. No country's tap-water production fell within 10 percent; the whole Netherlands produces 1,160 million cubic metres a year against the city's 1,382.

check.finding: The caveat's central claim -- "The Central Park Reservoir holds one billion gallons: the city empties it every day" -- is not true. The Central Park Conservancy confirms the reservoir "ceased providing water to New Yorkers in 1993," is purely ornamental today, and if pressed into service now "would only be able to supply New Yorkers with enough fresh water for about one day." Nobody empties it daily; it just sits full and unused. The 1-billion-gallon figure that's actually true daily is systemwide supply from the upstate reservoir network, not this specific decommissioned reservoir. The caveat conflates a coincidental capacity match with an operational fact.
check.conflict: The same Mumbai article also states current daily demand has "surged to 4,463 MLD" (vs. the 4,000 MLD actually supplied) -- a bigger, more current figure for how much water Mumbai needs, from the same source, not used.
check.resolution: The false claim is gone. The Central Park Reservoir was taken out of service in 1993 and supplies nobody; the line now says so instead of implying the city drains it daily.

items.sentence: has as many murders a year as Houston has homicides
items.caveat: Houston counts homicides, which take in negligent manslaughter and other killings that New York City's murder figure leaves out, so the true gap is wider. Houston has 2.4 million people to New York City's 8.5 million, so its rate is about three times higher.

nyc.label: Murders in New York City, 2025
nyc.quote: Across the city, murder declined by 20.2% (305 vs. 382), with 77 fewer murders compared to 2024.

match.label: Homicides in Houston, 2025
match.quote: Between 2024 and 2025, the number of homicides reported to the Houston Police Department declined from 331 to 272, according to year-end data gleaned through an open records request.

items.note: NYPD year-end 2025 release (murder and non-negligent manslaughter); Houston Police Department 2025 homicide count obtained by the Houston Chronicle through a records request and syndicated on Yahoo News. Houston is 11 percent lower, the widest gap on this page; Memphis (235) and Philadelphia (222) were further off. Populations from Census Vintage 2024.

check.finding: The caveat notes the terms differ ("Houston's count is homicides reported to its police") but doesn't disclose the substance of that difference. Per Houston Chronicle reporting, HPD's 272 "homicides" figure includes cases classified as murder AND both negligent and non-negligent manslaughter (justifiable homicides are tracked separately and excluded). NYC's 305 "murder" figure is Murder and Non-Negligent Manslaughter only, per UCR/Penal Law classification, which excludes negligent manslaughter. Houston's broader category is being compared to NYC's narrower one, and Houston's true murder-equivalent count is likely somewhat below 272 -- meaning the real gap between the two cities is probably larger than the 305-vs-272 comparison suggests.
check.resolution: The caveat now says what the difference is, not just that there is one: Houston counts homicides, which take in negligent manslaughter and other killings that New York City's murder figure leaves out.
